A_target.statement:
Let $g$ be [[Definition:Continuously Differentiable|continuously differentiable]] on $\closedint a b$ and $f$ [[Definition:Continuous Real Function|continuous]] on $\map g {\closedint a b}$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \int_a^b \map f {\map g x} \map {g'} x \rd x = \int_{\map g a}^{\map g b} \map f u \rd u$

B_source.statement:
Let $F$ and $g$ be [[Definition:Differentiable Real Function|differentiable]].
Then:
:$\map {\paren {F \circ g}'} x = \map {F'} {\map g x} \map {g'} x$

substitutions.the composite being differentiated: an antiderivative of the outer function composed with the inner one
substitutions.the two factors produced by the chain ru: the integrand appearing in the substitution formula
substitutions.the endpoints of the interval: their images under the inner function

derived.integrating the chain rule identity: the antiderivative evaluated at the transformed endpoints
derived.recognizing the boundary values: the integral of the outer function over the image interval

object_map.reformulation: Recognize the integrand as the derivative produced by the chain rule, so integration undoes the composition.

validity_conditions: The outer function must be continuous so that an antiderivative exists, and the inner function continuously differentiable so the chain rule applies.

The integral over the image interval is taken between the images of the endpoints, with orientation preserved; if the inner function is not monotone the image is still traversed with correct signed multiplicity.
Rewriting the boundary values as an integral over the image interval uses the fundamental theorem of calculus again, now applied to the outer function.
proof_plan:
Let $F$ be a [[Definition:Primitive (Calculus)|primitive]] of $f$.
By the [[Chain Rule for Derivatives]]:
:$\map {\paren {F \circ g}'} x = \map f {\map g x} \map {g'} x$
The right hand side is the integrand of the substitution formula.

Integrating over $\closedint a b$ and applying the [[Fundamental Theorem of Calculus]]:
:$\displaystyle \int_a^b \map f {\map g x} \map {g'} x \rd x = \map F {\map g b} - \map F {\map g a}$

Again by the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus:
:$\map F {\map g b} - \map F {\map g a} = \displaystyle \int_{\map g a}^{\map g b} \map f u \rd u$
which is [[Integration by Substitution]].
{{qed}}
